text.paragraph: New patient with a non-healing sore on the lower lip and chest tightness on exertion: lip biopsy, coronary disease assessment, secondary prevention, and care preferences. Concerns: A sore on his lower lip has not healed for three months, and he wants to know whether it is cancer; He gets tight in the chest walking uphill and wants to stay active enough to keep coaching; He wants his care to respect who he is and to be told plainly about costs and choices. [S]

list.item: Non-healing lesion of the left lower lip for about three months: a 1.2 cm firm, crusted ulcer on the vermilion that bleeds when touched, on a background of dry, scaly lips from years of outdoor work; no numbness of the lip or chin and no palpable neck nodes. Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma; incisional biopsy taken today and otolaryngology consultation booked: resolved, confirmed [S]

Chronic coronary disease with stable exertional angina: tightness in the chest when walking uphill or carrying loads for about a year, relieved by two or three minutes of rest, never at rest; heart attack eight years ago, treated in hospital, with no regular care or medicines since. Resting ECG: sinus rhythm with Q waves in the inferior leads. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heart attacks: active, confirmed [S]

Squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lip (external vermilion): invasive, well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma on incisional biopsy; 1.2 cm, no palpable neck nodes; clinical stage T1 N0 (AJCC 8th edition, lip and oral cavity). Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented lip cancer: active, confirmed [S]

Acute low back strain after lifting bags of infield clay while preparing a ball field: pain across the lower back without leg pain, numbness, weakness, or bladder or bowel change; no red flags apart from a recent, fully excised early lip cancer; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]
Actinic keratoses: two rough, scaly patches on the backs of the hands, in sun-damaged skin; treated with cryotherapy: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Former Olympic champion and professional football and baseball player. Since then has worked in construction, security work and film work, served in the merchant marine, and now speaks at schools and community events and coaches young athletes [S]
Sun exposure: decades of outdoor training, play and construction work, rarely with a hat or lip protection; two blistering sunburns of the lips that he remembers [S]
Tobacco: smoked about a pack of cigarettes a day from his twenties until his heart attack eight years ago (about 35 pack-years); no smokeless tobacco since [S]
Alcohol: drank heavily in earlier years and cut down on his own after his heart attack; now one or two beers on some weekends (AUDIT-C 2) [S]

Enrolled member of the Sac and Fox Nation; lives with his wife in a small house he rents; has health insurance through a public program. Asked how he would like his care organized, he said he wanted his care here and would like information about Sac and Fox Nation and Indian Health Service health programs before deciding whether to use them [S]

Strengths and supports: lifelong athlete who still walks and throws a ball with the young people he coaches; speaks about education and opportunity for Native youth; proud of his family and community [S]

tr.td: New patient with a non-healing sore on the lower lip and chest tightness on exertion: lip biopsy, coronary disease assessment, secondary prevention, and care preferences

Coronary disease review in cardiac rehabilitation, lipid recheck after ezetimibe, and lip surveillance
Four months after surgery: lip and neck surveillance, coronary disease review, and screening results
Same-day sick visit for low back pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Incisional biopsy of the lip lesion today, with pathology; sun protection for the lips and skin (lip balm with SPF 30 or higher, a broad-brimmed hat); dental review
Otolaryngology (head and neck surgery) consultation for a suspected lip cancer: staging, treatment, management of the neck, and surveillance

Secondary prevention for chronic coronary disease: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after starting and a goal LDL below 55 mg/dL, metoprolol succinate for angina, sublingual nitroglycerin with written instructions, blood pressure below 130/80, an echocardiogram to measure heart function before surgery, and staying tobacco-free
Cardiac rehabilitation once the lip wound has healed: up to 36 supervised exercise and education sessions for stable angina, with nutrition, activity, and risk-factor coaching

Care organized around his choices: information about Sac and Fox Nation health services and Indian Health Service, tribal, and urban Indian health programs, help to use them if he wishes, and room for any traditional or spiritual practices he chooses; costs and options explained plainly

V-excision of the lip cancer under local anesthesia with 5 to 10 mm clinical margins and frozen-section margin control, primary closure; contrast CT of the neck before surgery; no elective neck dissection if the final depth of invasion is small; aspirin and metoprolol continued through surgery

Surveillance after lip cancer: history and examination of the lips, mouth and neck every 1 to 3 months in the first year, every 2 to 6 months in the second, every 4 to 8 months in years 3 to 5, then yearly; whole-skin examination; dental care; tobacco-free; imaging only for symptoms or findings
Ezetimibe 10 mg daily added to atorvastatin because LDL was 68 mg/dL, above the goal of 55 mg/dL, with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks later
Lip cancer removed with clear margins and no recurrence on surveillance through four months
Excised with clear margins; no recurrence or neck nodes at four months
LDL cholesterol below 55 mg/dL on secondary prevention
LDL 51 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg and ezetimibe 10 mg
Complete cardiac rehabilitation and walk uphill without angina
30 of 36 sessions done; no angina and no nitroglycerin use for two months
Stay tobacco-free and protect his lips and skin from the sun
Tobacco-free; lip balm with sunscreen and a hat used daily

list.item: Independent; walks a mile on level ground without symptoms; stops on hills because of chest tightness [S]
